subject: Private offer: SKU bundle packaging + channel discount slicing
messages:
From: Alan Pritchard <alan@cloudbridge.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
Cc: CloudBridge Channel Ops <channel-ops@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer questions — bundling and partner margin allocation

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick intro on Friday. We're running a deal team at Acme and are evaluating a combined GCP + Azure private-offer bundle that includes Redwood hosted inference with a 3-year commitment. A couple of items we need clarity on before we build our mutual action plan (MAP):

- Can Redwood support a single private-offer SKU that maps to two marketplace SKUs (GCP + Azure) while preserving a single list price on the offer? Any limitations from the marketplace side we should anticipate?
- What flexibility do you have on how partner margin is allocated? Our channel team prefers a waterfall split where the partner gets an increasing uplift at commit milestones (e.g., first-year baseline then step-ups as ARR thresholds are hit).
- We'll need a draft margin model for internal sign-off (partner uplift, Redwood net rev, taxes/withholdings).

I've attached a short summary of the customer's required packaging (ACME_private_offer_draft.pdf) and a rough target net price range. Can you confirm who on your side drives the channel margin waterfall and whether Redwood can absorb partial discounts during the pilot?

Happy to jump on a 30 min call this week.

Best,
Alan
Alan Pritchard
Director, Strategic Channels
CloudBridge
[Attachment: ACME_private_offer_draft.pdf (PDF)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private offer questions — bundling and partner margin allocation

Team — forwarding CloudBridge's note. Quick summary of asks: single-offer across clouds, partner waterfall margin, and an initial margin model for their procurement. They specifically called out absorbing partial discount during a pilot.

Questions / ask to owners:
- Marcus: can you produce a partner margin waterfall that shows net Redwood rev by tier (0-250k/250-1M/1M+) and a version where we front-load a pilot concession for 3 months? Include tax/marketplace fees assumptions.
- Ben: confirm whether we can create a cross-cloud private offer (single list price) or if marketplaces will force separate SKUs/offers. If separate, we need a routing plan (GCP vs Azure) and an ops note.
- Irene: partner agreement risk — if we give an uplift to the partner that's funded from Redwood during pilot, do we need any special contract language or escrow to protect net rev?

Proposed next steps: Marcus prepares margin model + two scenarios; Ben and I join a sync with CloudBridge Wednesday 11am PT if that works.

Thanks — Steph

Stephanie Nguyen | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0187

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer questions — bundling and partner margin allocation

Attaching a quick model (margin_model_v2.xlsx) and summarizing assumptions here.

Top-line model notes:
- Base list price (single-offer list) mapped to two underlying billing SKUs (GCP, Azure). Marketplace requires per-cloud invoicing but we can present a single offer to the buyer and map behind the scenes. Ops will need routing rules; Ben please confirm the SKU mapping workflow.
- Partner waterfall proposal (net Redwood revenue perspective):
  * Tier A (0–$250k yearly): partner rebate = 12% of list, Redwood net = 88% before marketplace fees
  * Tier B ($250k–$1M): partner rebate steps to 18% (uplift kicks in at 250k GCMA ARR)
  * Tier C (>$1M): partner rebate 22% (accelerator)
- Pilot concession option: for first 90 days Redwood funds 50% of partner rebate (i.e., partner receives the same payout but Redwood nets less); modeled as a short-term marketing allowance that phases out.
- Marketplace/Tax drag: assume 5% marketplace fee + 3% expected tax/withholding. Include an addendum line for possible VAT in EU scenarios (not relevant to US deal).

Constraints and risks:
- We can do the pilot concession but we need a CLAR clause in SOW that caps Redwood's total exposure to X dollars (we'll set X based on the model).
- If CloudBridge requests list-price erosion (lowering list price permanently), that materially reduces headroom — prefer they take credits/commitment tier discounts instead of cutting list.

I'll leave the spreadsheet in the Drive folder and flag cells that feed the SOW.

[Attachment: margin_model_v2.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet)]

Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
To: Alan Pritchard <alan@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: CloudBridge Channel Ops <channel-ops@cloudbridge.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer questions — bundling and partner margin allocation

Alan — thanks for the clear note and the draft. We've reviewed internally and can do the following: 

1) Packaging: we can present a single private-offer to Acme and map it to per-cloud billing SKUs internally; marketplace billing will remain per-cloud but the buyer sees one offer. Ben will share the routing diagram during the call.

2) Partner waterfall & pilot structure: Marcus attached a margin model with two scenarios. Proposal for moving forward:
   - Pilot (90 days): Redwood funds 50% of partner uplift for the pilot period so CloudBridge receives a 15% effective partner payout on initial ARR (modeled as a marketing allowance). Redwood net rev during the pilot will be reduced as modeled but capped at $45k exposure for the pilot (see model).
   - Post-pilot: waterfall as modeled — 12% / 18% / 22% by tier (0–250k/250k–1M/>1M).

3) Contract and SOW: Irene recommends a 90-day concession addendum that amortizes the pilot allowance and includes a cap on Redwood's allowance exposure; she'll draft language and circulate an appendix.

4) Ops: Ben, please confirm the SKU mapping process and whether we need two separate private-offer entries in the marketplaces or if we can route one offer to two billing SKUs.

Next steps:
- Ben to confirm ops routing + any marketplace constraints (by EOD Tuesday).
- Irene to draft pilot concession addendum (by EOD Tuesday).
- Marcus to finalize model and add a second scenario where Redwood does NOT fund pilot concessions (for comparison).
- Proposed sync with CloudBridge: Wed 11:00 AM PT (invite sent).

If that looks good to you, Alan, we'll lock the call and share the Drive link and a DocuSign preview for the concession appendix.
